subject: Publisher onboarding: offer resilience checklist & tenant-proofing plan
messages:
From: Lina Moreno <lina.moreno@microsoft.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: contoso-partner-team@contoso.com
Date: 2026-10-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Azure onboarding: resilience & tenant hardening questions

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the office hours yesterday. Per our call, the marketplace intake team asked for two items before we can move your private offer to the validation queue: a concise mapping between your product SKUs and Azure entitlements, and a short checklist that describes how you bootstrap a tenant in customer subscriptions (identity, secrets, telemetry).

I attached a template that usually speeds review — filled-in examples help the engineering gatekeepers. Can you confirm whether your offer needs delegated resource permissions (SPN with role assignment), or if you’ll use customer-managed identities? Also, are there any custom ARM hooks during provisioning that might cause the portal smoke tests to fail?

If helpful, we can do a 30-minute technical sync with the validation team Tue/Wed.

Thanks,
Lina
Marketplace PM — Microsoft Cloud Partner Program

Attachments (2): rdw-offer-resilience-checklist.xlsx, entitlement-mapping-v1.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Moreno <lina.moreno@microsoft.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-08T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Azure onboarding: resilience & tenant hardening questions

Hi Lina —

Appreciate the checklist and the template. Quick answers up front:
- We prefer customer-assigned managed identities for isolation; however, some legacy customers still use SPNs. We support both patterns.
- We do not run custom ARM hooks that modify subscription-level resources. Our bootstrap uses ARM templates to create deployment-scoped resources (resource group + deployment) and then calls our onboarding service via MSI.
- Portal smoke tests we’ve seen fail when RBAC propagation lags for new role assignments (15–30s). We added a retry loop but will call that out in the checklist.

I attached an initial pass at the entitlement mapping (entitlement-mapping-v1.pdf) and a draft resilience checklist; Marissa will follow up with procurement-related evidence.

We’re available Wed 10/13 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 10/14 14:00–15:00 PT for a joint sync with the validation engineers. Which works for the team?

—Karthik
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Moreno <lina.moreno@microsoft.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-09T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Azure onboarding: resilience & tenant hardening questions

Lina / team —

Adding the procurement perspective: we have the commercial attachment (invoice samples, EULA) ready; I'll upload the redlines to the docsend link and share the DocuSign envelope for the publisher agreement. For the validation packet, can you confirm the expected evidence for data residency (where the offer configuration is stored) and the retention policy for operation logs? We keep audit logs in our control plane for 90 days by default, with options for enterprise customers to extend to 365 days.

I also flagged the RBAC propagation note in the checklist and added an explicit step: after creating role assignment, pause 30s and verify token acquisition. That should address the portal flakiness.

Marissa
Sr. Product Manager, GTM Operations — Redwood Inference

Attachments: none (procurement docs to follow via DocuSign)

From: Lina Moreno <lina.moreno@microsoft.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: contoso-partner-team@contoso.com
Date: 2026-10-10T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Azure onboarding: resilience & tenant hardening questions

Thanks — helpful summary.

Two quick asks before the sync:
1) Can you add a short runbook section that explains your fallback if a tenant bootstrap fails mid-run (idempotency, rollbacks, cleanup)? The validation engineers will test failure modes.
2) Please include example Azure activity log excerpts (anonymized) showing role assignment and MSI usage. That helps the security reviewer.

Wed 10/13 10:00 PT works for the validation sync. I'll send a calendar invite for 30m and loop in two engineers from the validation queue.

Lina

On a related note — contoso mentioned they want to map two entitlements to a single SKU in the portal. If that mapping changes billing or co-sell tagging, we need an explicit note because Marketplace entitlement-to-billing mapping impacts co-sell attribution.

Lina

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Moreno <lina.moreno@microsoft.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T15:46:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Azure onboarding: resilience & tenant hardening questions

Lina / team —

Thanks — we've updated the checklist with:
- a 3-step idempotent rollback flow when bootstrap hits an error (delete partial resources by deployment name, revoke temporary tokens, mark the tenant as "bootstrap-failed" in our control plane and surface a retry endpoint),
- anonymized activity log snippets (attached) showing role assignment and MSI token retrieval,
- explicit note that mapping two entitlements to one SKU will not change billing units for customers but will affect co-sell tagging; we created a short mapping table and flagged it for you in entitlement-mapping-v1.pdf.

I uploaded the latest artifacts to the DocSend link and created a quick Jira ticket for the validation team: https://jira.redwood.ai/SEC-4321. We'll be prepared for Wed 10/13 10:00 PT.

—Karthik

Attachments (2): rdw-offer-resilience-checklist.xlsx, entitlement-mapping-v1.pdf
